page: Amazon Web Services r5a.xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and first-generation AMD EPYC 7571 processors. Running on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 4 virtual CPUs across 2 physical cores clocked at a base speed of 2.5 GHz with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture comprises 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 8 MB L3 cache, complemented by baseline instruction support including AVX, AES, SHA-NI, and BMI2.

Hardware allocation includes 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing an ample 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance comes without bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, necessitating reliance on network-attached storage over an Elastic Block Store interface. Network connectivity is rated at a 1 Gbps baseline. Because the memory allocation is large relative to compute, memory-resident tasks can leverage adequate capacity without incurring the higher cost of compute-dense instances.

Benchmark evaluations reveal modest processing throughput aligned with older CPU architectures. Geekbench testing records a single-core score of 711.0 and a multi-core score of 1709.0, both placing in the bottom tier of evaluated systems. Similarly, stress-ng multi-core testing yields 1178.65 points. Memory bandwidth is measured at 25.43 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 12.49 GB/sec for writes. PassMark cryptographic tests score 3238.05 due to hardware AES acceleration, whereas general database operations rate lower at 990.98.

Given its high RAM-to-CPU ratio and modest compute power, the r5a.xlarge serves workloads requiring moderate in-memory capacity with low compute intensity. Typical deployments include Redis caching layers, background queuing systems, development databases, and mid-tier analytics engines where cost-effective memory footprint takes priority over compute execution speed.

Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with the x86_64 architecture, this instance offers an 8.0 GB RAM-to-vCPU ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU accelerators, relying on remote block storage and a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate modest compute and memory bandwidth throughput, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 1709.0 and uncached memory read bandwidth of 25.43 GB/sec, though hardware crypto acceleration yields average performance in encryption benchmarks. The r5a.xlarge provides an economical solution for memory-heavy, low-to-moderate compute applications such as distributed caching, in-memory data structures, and intermediate data staging environments.
